chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr and Al-Fadl and Muhammad and Bureyd, from one of the two (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the grandfather with the brothers (from the father) becomes like one of the brothers, whatever number they reach.

He said, I said, 'A man left his brother from his father and mother, and his grandfather,' or I said, 'Left his grandfather, and his brother from his father and mother.' He said, 'The wealth is divided between them, and even if there were two brothers or a hundred thousand, so for him is like the share of one of the brothers.'

He said, I said, 'A man left his grandfather and his sister.' So he said, 'For the male is like the portion of the two females, and if there were two sisters, so the half is for the grandfather and the other half for the two sisters, and if they were more than that, then upon this calculation, and if he left brothers and sisters from a father and mother, or from a father and a grandfather, so the grandfather is one of the brothers, so the wealth is between them, for the male is like the portion of the two females.'
Zurara said, 'This is from what is not taken against me; I have heard it from his father, and from him before that, and there is no doubt or difference with us regarding that.'

key_terms.الْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ الْأَبِ: Paternal brothers (half-siblings sharing the same father)
key_terms.حَظّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: The portion of two females (double the share of one female)

ai.seo_question: How is the grandfather's share calculated in relation to brothers and sisters in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential position that the grandfather (al-Jadd) is treated as a single brother (khalif al-akh) in inheritance, a view supported by the consensus of the Imams as noted by Zurara. It details specific distribution scenarios, such as when the grandfather competes with full siblings or sisters, establishing that he receives a share equivalent to one brother regardless of the total number of siblings. This ruling resolves the historical juristic debate regarding whether the grandfather inherits as a distinct category or merges with the sibling class.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Bukeyr and Al Fazl and Muhammad and Bureyd, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The grandfather is with the brothers from the father, becoming like one from the brothers, whatever (number) they reach’.  
He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘A man left his brother from this father and his mother, and his grandfather’, or I said, ‘Left his grandfather, and his brother from this father and his mother’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth is (divided) between them, even if there were two brothers or a hundred thousand, so for his would be like the share of one of the brothers’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘A man left his grandfather and his sister’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the male is like the portion of two females, and even if there were two sisters, so the half would be for the grandfather, and the other half for the two sisters, even if they were to be more than that. Thus, it is upon this calculation, if he were to leave brothers and sisters from the father and mother, or from the father, and a grandfather, so, for the grandfather is one (with the) brothers. So the wealth is (divided) between them, for the male being the like of the portion of the two females’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah and Bukayr and al- Fudayl and Muhammad and Burayd who has narrated the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘ Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said,
‘The grandfather with brothers from the father’s side become like one of the brothers regardless of how many they are.’

He (the narrator) has said that I asked, ‘A man has left his brother from his mother and father and his grandfather’, or I asked, ‘He has left his grandfather, his brother from his father and mother.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The legacy is given to them, regardless, one or one hundred thousand he (grandfather) receives the share of one brother.’

I then asked, ‘A man has left behind his grandfather and his sister.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The male receives like the share of two females. If they are two sisters then one- half is for grandfather and the other one-half for the two sisters. However, if they are more, it then is like the above calculation, if he leaves brothers and sisters from father and mother and grandfather then the grandfather is like one of the brothers and the legacy among them is distributed, each male receiving twice the share of a female.’”
Zurarah has said, ‘This is what I cannot be questioned for because I heard it from his father and from him (the Imam) before and we have no doubt about it or differences.’”
